title: WHEN TRUTH IS DISMISSED AS LAZINESS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh said, "Lazy, that's what you are—lazy! That is why you keep saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.' Now get to work. You will not be given any straw, yet you must produce your full quota of bricks."" - Exodus 5:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is no reasoning with him. Pharaoh does not engage with a single point they raised. He simply calls them lazy and repeats the order.

Calling people lazy is easier than examining an unjust system. It shifts the blame downward and protects the one in power. Every generation has heard it.

If you have ever been unfairly labelled — lazy, difficult, over-sensitive, too religious — you know how it stings, especially when the accusation comes from someone with authority over you. There is often no way to defend yourself.

Jesus was called a glutton, a drunkard, a friend of sinners, and worse (Mt 11:19). He did not spend His life correcting the record. When He was insulted, He did not retaliate, but entrusted Himself to the One who judges justly (1 Pet 2:23).

That is where we must land. Not everyone will assess us fairly. God always will. His verdict is the one that stands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What unfair label am I carrying, and have I handed it to God?
2. Do I judge others quickly without understanding their circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am misjudged, keep me from bitterness. I entrust my reputation to You, the only fair Judge. Amen.
